chapter_metadata.title: Single Use Bronchoscopes
chapter_metadata.reference: Principles and Practice of Interventional Pulmonology, 2025

definitions.definition: Single‑use flexible bronchoscope; pre‑sterilized, intended for one patient use.
Reusable flexible bronchoscope; requires decontamination/reprocessing between patients.
Bronchoalveolar lavage; sampling alveolar secretions for analysis.
Life Cycle Assessment; evaluation of environmental impacts across a product’s life.

technology_and_technique.summary: SUFB now in later generations with improved imaging and angulation; vendors include Ambu, Boston Scientific, TSC Broncoflex, Karl Storz, Pentax, Vathin, Verathon.
SUFB connect to small portable reusable screens (vendor‑specific) enabling out‑of‑suite and emergency use; images/videos easily saved.

clinical_procedures.name: Diagnostic uses
steps: BAL and washings via working channel.
Brushings and transbronchial biopsies per protocol.
clinical_procedures.notes: Noninferior to RFB for routine bronchoscopy, BAL, and biopsy in clinical studies.

clinical_procedures.name: Therapeutic uses
steps: Support for tumor debulking (mechanical/energy adjuncts), stent deployment, foreign body removal.
Guidance for percutaneous tracheostomy; BLVR tools; bronchial thermoplasty; fiducial placement.

recommendations: Consider SUFB to reduce cross‑contamination risk in mechanically ventilated, immunosuppressed, or infectious patients.
Avoid reprocessing of SUFB; do not reuse even on the same patient.
Use SUFB for parallel throughput, off‑hours availability, and training/simulation to reduce RFB damage.
Choose device mix (SUFB vs RFB) based on annual procedure volume and institutional logistics.
Perform local LCA when feasible; consider production, transport, reprocessing inputs, and disposal pathways.
Note that published LCAs provide conflicting conclusions depending on assumptions and processes.

increases: Biofilms and channel damage in RFB
decreases: Use of SUFB for high‑risk patients/procedures

environmental.notes: Net impact depends on local energy mix, reprocessing, and waste disposal (incineration vs recycling pathways).

decreases: Avoided repairs, reprocessing labor, infection‑related costs; economies of scale may alter pricing

management: Use SUFB in ICU/emergency/contagious settings to lower cross‑contamination risk.
Use RFB where high throughput and established reprocessing yield lower per‑case cost; protect against biofilm/repair issues.

points: SUFB reduce cross‑contamination risk and increase availability; newer generations approach RFB performance.
Cost‑effectiveness and environmental impact depend on local volumes and practices; LCAs are mixed.
Standardized multicenter LCAs and clinical trials will clarify optimal device mix.
